name: Anthracosuchus
sum: Dyrosaurid with an extremely short, stout snout, from the Paleocene Cerrejón Formation of Colombia.
holotype: UF/IGM 67, a nearly complete, dorsoventrally compressed skull with 9 ribs, 7 vertebrae and unidentified bones.
material: Four specimens with partial skulls come from the Cerrejón mine; referred specimens UF/IGM 69 and 70 are known only from cranial material.
biology: Differs from other dyrosaurids in its extremely short snout, widely spaced eye sockets with bony protuberances, and smooth, thick osteoderms.
author: Hastings et al. 2015
